title: Keep USB audio inputs without connector detection available
problem: USBAudio2-ACX advertises jack detection on endpoints whose USB terminals have no connector control, causing a selected input behind a hardware selector to appear unavailable in the legacy Windows sound panel.
reproduce: Install the yamaha-main driver for a USB Audio 2 device with a Selector Unit, select an input such as Aux In in Windows Settings, then open the Recording page in mmsys.cpl; the selected endpoint says Currently unavailable and its level meter stays idle.
acceptance: Dummy jacks for terminals without connector control are advertised as static, connector-controlled physical jacks retain presence detection, and the selected MUX input remains available in mmsys.cpl.
repair: Configure the no-connector-control dummy jack with no detection flag or presence callback while preserving its connected state and leaving the physical jack path unchanged.

verification.limitations: BCL verifies the pinned production source is red before the change and green after it, and that connector-controlled jacks retain detection. The Windows kernel driver has not been built or installed by BCL; the final UI and meter behavior require the reporter's Sound Blaster G3.
verification.ownerCheck: Build and install the candidate USBAudio2-ACX driver on the reported Windows setup. Select Aux In, open mmsys.cpl Recording, and confirm it shows Default Device with an active level meter. Repeat with Microphone, What U Hear and SPDIF In, then check a device with real connector detection still changes availability when unplugged.

selection.reason: A same-day report reproduces on x64 and Arm64 and on two USB Audio 2 devices. The exact yamaha-main revision is supplied, and the reporter can immediately validate the driver on a Sound Blaster G3.

publish.commitMessage: Fix: Mark endpoints without connector control as static
